_comment: What a task description says differently for a language (pipeline/run_codex.py, template()). Chinese is not here: its task descriptions are the templates as they are, as in the first round. sentence and graph: an annotated sentence of the language's shared-task training data, shown as the example; doc: the document-level graph shown with it (doc_is_illustration: made here to show the format, the training sentence has none).

en.name: English
en.sentence: Lindsay left in order to eat lunch .
en.graph:
(s1l / leave-02
        :ARG0 (s1p / person
            :name (s1n / name
                :op1 "Lindsay"))
        :aspect performance
        :purpose (s1e / eat-01
            :ARG0 s1p
            :ARG1 (s1l2 / lunch)
            :aspect performance))

cs.name: Czech
cs.graph:
(s1d1 / dodat-005
        :aspect performance
        :modal-strength full-affirmative
        :ARG0 (s1e1 / person
            :refer-number singular
            :refer-person 3rd)
        :ARG1 (s1b1 / have-degree-91
            :aspect state
            :modal-strength full-affirmative
            :quote s1d1
            :ARG1 (s1p1 / pole)
            :ARG2 (s1v1 / volný)
            :ARG3 (s1v2 / více)
            :temporal (s1t1 / teď)))
cs.clause: (its lemma, with the frame number the Czech data uses: `dodat-005` for "dodal")
cs.notes: An event concept is the verb's lemma with the three-digit frame number the Czech data uses (`dodat-005`, `stát-se-001`; a reflexive verb is written with its particle, `stát-se`). Other words are their lemmas. The Czech training annotations mark `:modal-strength` on the event itself and have only coreference at the document level: follow them in the sentence graphs, and give the document-level relations in the format below all the same.
cs.tools: There is no frame lexicon for Czech in this directory: `tools/propbank_lookup.py` answers that it has nothing. Take a predicate's frame number and its roles from the training annotations: search `tools/search_annotations.py` for the lemma (for example `dodat-`) and follow what they do. The Czech training data is large (160,000 sentences, most of them converted automatically): a search takes a few seconds.

la.name: Latin
la.sentence: Intra eas silvas hostes in occulto sese continebant
la.graph:
(s1c1 / contineo
        :aspect activity
        :place (s1s1 / silva
            :refer-number plural
            :mod (s1i1 / is))
        :ARG0 (s1h1 / hostis
            :refer-number plural)
        :manner (s1o1 / occultum
            :refer-number singular)
        :ARG1 s1h1)
la.notes: Concepts are Latin lemmas (`contineo`, `hostis`, `silva`). There are no frame files for Latin here, so a sense number cannot be looked up: write the lemma, with the numbered roles as the training annotations use them.
la.tools: There is no frame lexicon for Latin in this directory: `tools/propbank_lookup.py` answers that it has nothing. `tools/search_annotations.py` has about 1,000 Latin training sentences (Caesar, Cicero, Sallust), converted automatically: sentence graphs without sense numbers and without document-level relations. Use them for the concepts and roles of a construction; for the document-level relations rely on the guidelines.

arp.name: Arapaho
arp.graph:
(s1h / hii-00
        :actor s1p
        :theme (s1h2 / hehno'uukohei-00
            :actor (s1p / person
                :refer-person 1st
                :refer-number singular)
            :start (s1p3 / place)
            :goal (s1p2 / place)
            :temporal (s1h3 / hohkonee)
            :mod (s1h4 / hee)
            :aspect performance
            :quote s1h)
        :aspect performance)
arp.clause: (for an Arapaho verb its stem with `-00`: `hii-00` for "nih'iit")
arp.notes: There are no frame files for Arapaho. An event concept is the verb stem with `-00` (`hii-00`, `hee3-00`), and its participants take the general participant roles of the guidelines (`:actor`, `:undergoer`, `:theme`, `:recipient`, `:experiencer`, `:stimulus`, ...) instead of numbered roles. Other words are written as their stem or as the sentence writes them; the training annotations show how a word form is reduced to its stem.
arp.tools: There is no frame lexicon for Arapaho in this directory: `tools/propbank_lookup.py` answers that it has nothing. `tools/search_annotations.py` has about 350 Arapaho training sentences: search them for the word forms and stems of the sentence, and follow what they do.

nv.name: Navajo
nv.sentence: Haalá ’áhoodzaa shą́ą́’ dohníi ni’ dííniid Bilį́į́’ Łizhinii yę́ę
nv.graph:
(s1d / dííniid
        :aspect activity
        :actor (s1p / person)
        :theme (s1d2 / dohníi
            :aspect activity
            :actor (s1p2 / person
                :refer-person 2nd
                :refer-number dual)
            :theme (s1x / ’áhoodzaa
                :aspect performance
                :undergoer (s1h / haalá))))
nv.clause: (in Navajo the word as the sentence writes it: `dííniid`)
nv.notes: There are no frame files for Navajo. A concept is the word as the sentence writes it, without a sense number (`dííniid`, `dohníi`), and the participants of an event take the general participant roles of the guidelines (`:actor`, `:undergoer`, `:theme`, `:recipient`, `:experiencer`, `:stimulus`, ...) instead of numbered roles.
nv.tools: There is no frame lexicon for Navajo in this directory: `tools/propbank_lookup.py` answers that it has nothing. `tools/search_annotations.py` has about 340 Navajo training sentences: search them for the words of the sentence, and follow what they do.

        :ARG0 (s1p / person

it.notes: There are no frame files and no training annotations for Italian. Follow the guidelines for a language without frame files: an event concept is the lemma without a sense number (`mangiare`), and its participants take the general participant roles (`:actor`, `:undergoer`, `:theme`, `:recipient`, `:experiencer`, `:stimulus`, ...) instead of numbered roles. The example under Output format is an English sentence annotated with English frame files; it shows the format only.
it.tools: There is no frame lexicon for Italian in this directory (`tools/propbank_lookup.py` answers that it has nothing), and `tools/search_annotations.py` has no Italian sentences: it answers that there is no data. Only `tools/search_guidelines.py` helps for this document.
